chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, God will hold the servants strictly accountable in the Reckoning on the Day of Resurrection according to the measure of the intellect He gave them in this world.

key_terms.الْعُقُول: Plural of 'aql (intellect/reason) — in Shia theology, the 'aql is both the faculty of reason and the moral compass by which humans are held responsible
key_terms.يُدَاقُّ: From daqq/mudaqqa: to examine minutely, to hold strictly accountable, to be exact in reckoning — implies meticulous divine scrutiny

ai.seo_question: How does Islam determine the level of accountability on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) teaches that divine accountability on the Day of Judgment is proportional to the intellect God has bestowed upon each person in this world. This hadith, found in the chapter on the intellect ('aql) in al-Kafi, establishes a principle of divine justice: those given greater rational capacity bear greater moral responsibility. The original Shia scholarly audience would have understood this as affirming both God's mercy (not holding people accountable beyond their capacity) and the high esteem in which 'aql is held as a divine gift.
